Maya (PM): quick sync — we need to finalize prioritization for the structured-output / tool-calling PRD. customer asks + launch criteria + edgecases. can we lock scope today?
Sanjay (Eng): can we split into two tracks: (A) strict-schema mode for enterprise customers, (B) best-effort mode for public hosted API. different validation semantics, different rollout.
Lew (Eng-ML): +1. Also suggest explicit metrics for rollout: parse_success_rate, fn_invocation_error_rate, avg_latency_p50/p95, and token-cost delta. need thresholds.
Olga (Design): keep UX fallback simple. if schema parse fails, show clear error + raw text output option. customers told Rahul they'd prefer predictable failures over silent incorrect calls.
Rahul (Customer Success): speaking of customers — ACME & FinLedger want strict enforcement + audit logs (who/when function called, payload). they'll pay for Dedicated/private but need deterministic behavior.
Maya (PM): Proposed minimal scope for M1: 1) function-calling with JSON-schema contract enforcement, 2) validation pipeline that can 1) reject, 2) coerce simple types, 3) emit warnings. M2: hooks for custom sanitizers and audit exports. Thoughts?
Sanjay (Eng): M1 is fine but 'coerce simple types' is risky. we should enumerate coercions (e.g., numeric strings -> number) and make them opt-in with "coerce=true" flag per route. default = strict reject.
Lew (Eng-ML): also handle partial responses: model may stream a truncated JSON. Validation should support incremental parsing + KV-cache safe checkpoints. If parse incomplete at stream end -> mark as truncated_error and optionally retry with backoff.
Maya (PM): good point. acceptance criteria suggestion:
- parse_success_rate >= 99.5% on internal test prompts at canary
- end-to-end function invocation success >= 99% (excluding customer-side function failures)
- latency regression <= 10% vs baseline
- no increase > 2% in token cost for typical prompts
Sanjay (Eng): add safety bucket: malformed payloads must not trigger sensitive tool calls. require a final validation gate before invoking any external action.
Olga (Design): UI needs to expose a clear "preview" of the parsed payload and a toggle for "invoke function" during canary. also show provenance: which model/version produced the payload.
Rahul (Customer Success): for enterprise SLAs add: retention of last 30 days of payload audit logs, with redaction options. legal asked for immutable event ids.
Lew (Eng-ML): edgecases list I've seen in prod: unknown enum values, extra_fields (forward vs strict), number overflow, date parsing ambiguities, locale-dependent formats, nested arrays with missing items, and streaming partial braces. we should add test vectors for each.
Maya (PM): let's capture those as acceptance tests. quick example for schema + test case:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "amount": { "type": "number" },
    "currency": { "type": "string", "enum": ["USD","EUR"] }
  },
  "required": ["amount","currency"]
}
```
Test: model returns `\{"amount\": \"100\", \"currency\": \"usd\"\}` -> behaviour: coerce? lowercase enum mismatch -> if coercion allowed, normalize to USD; else reject.
Sanjay (Eng): implementation note: add a validation mode header e.g., `X-Redwood-Validate: strict|coerce|warn` and a canary header `X-Redwood-Canary: true` so we can route telemetry separately.
triage-bot: linked RFC: https://redwood.company/rfc/312-structured-output-validation (added by triage-bot)
Olga (Design): accessibility note: error messages should be machine-parseable for automation, but human-friendly for debugging in Console.
Maya (PM): rollout plan proposal: canary on 5% of hosted -> monitor metrics for 48h -> expand to 30% -> enterprise beta gated by contract. if parse_success_rate drops below threshold OR fn_invocation_error_rate spikes -> auto-fallback to best-effort text-only routing.
Lew (Eng-ML): auto-fallback must preserve observability: record that fallback happened and why. also ensure KV cache invalidation strategies for retries.
Sanjay (Eng): dev checklist: unit validator lib, streaming parser, headers handling, canary router flag, metrics + alerts, audit log hook, CLI test harness. estimate: 6 dev-weeks for a baseline M1 (core team).
Maya (PM): OK. action items: @Sanjay own engineering plan + PRD section for dev checklist; @Lew write test vectors + streaming edgecases; @Olga mockups for Console preview + error states; @Rahul compile customer asks + contract clauses for audit retention. I'll draft launch criteria doc after these land.
Rahul (Customer Success): I'll ping ACME & FinLedger with the proposed scope and share opt-in timeline.
Sanjay (Eng): noted. will post initial draft of the engineering plan in this thread by EOD.
Maya (PM): thanks all. short follow-up: add an explicit acceptance criterion for "no silent function invocations" — any invocation must have a validated payload and an audit record.
Lew (Eng-ML): adding that to tests.
triage-bot: reminder set for 3 days to check back on PRD updates.
